stories.title: Private Investor Snags Brea Offices for $28M
stories.excerpt: CBRE facilitated the $27.8-million sale of Fairway Center II, a 135,308-square-foot office property located at 675 Placentia Ave. in Brea. CBRE represented the institutional seller. The Whittier Comstock, LLC, a subsidiary of MW Investment, LLC and owned by Matt Waken, acquired the property. CBRE’s Anthony DeLorenzo with National Office Properties, along with Sammy Cemo, Bryan Johnson and Jackson Marlow, represented the seller. Shaun Moothart and Andrew Post of CBRE’s Debt & Structured Finance practice secured the financing for the buyer. “Fairway Center II attracted significant interest amongst the investment and owner/user community alike,” said DeLorenzo. “We received multiple competitive offers from a variety of buyer profiles and awarded the property to a private investor within the first 30 days of marketing.” The property was 70.5% leased at the time of the sale. The property is anchored by the County of Orange, which occupies more than 61,000 square feet under a long-term lease. The post Private Investor Snags Brea Offices for $28M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MW Investment acquires 135K SF Brea office for $27.8M at 70.5% occupancy.
County of Orange anchors property with 61K SF long-term lease.
Private investor beat multiple offers; office conversion signals limited multifamily relevance.
stories.summary: MW Investment's subsidiary purchased Fairway Center II, a 135,308-square-foot office property in Brea, California, for $27.8 million. The property was 70.5% leased at sale, anchored by the County of Orange occupying 61,000 square feet under a long-term lease. The transaction closed within 30 days of marketing, attracting competitive bids from multiple buyer profiles.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily. Office product in Orange County (OC) continues to trade at distressed cap rates, but the County's long-term occupancy insulates this asset from conversion risk—unlikely to become an adaptive reuse multifamily development in near term.

stories.title: Vango Development Launches Leasing at Third Rutherford-Area Property
stories.excerpt: Vango Development has launched leasing at Parker East, a new five-story luxury rental community bringing 86 residences, indoor and outdoor lifestyle amenities and convenient mass-transit access to 263 Hackensack St. in East Rutherford, NJ. Located 0.2 miles from the Rutherford NJ TRANSIT station, Parker East offers one- and two-bedroom residences priced from $3,250. Immediate occupancy is available. The Taylor Lucyk Group is serving as the community’s exclusive leasing agent. “Parker East reflects our continued commitment to creating high-quality residential communities in well-connected neighborhoods,” said Van Golemis, CEO of Vango Development. “The combination of spacious residences, a strong amenity offering and a location close to both transit and Rutherford’s downtown gives residents the convenience and connectivity they’re looking for today.” The property is the latest addition to Vango’s growing portfolio in the area, following the development and lease-up of Parker 106 and Parker 118 in neighboring Rutherford. The post Vango Development Launches Leasing at Third Rutherford-Area Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Vango Development launches Parker East: 86 units, East Rutherford, NJ, 0.2 mi from transit.
Rents from $3,250 for one/two-bedroom; immediate occupancy available.
Third Vango property in Rutherford; transit-proximate infill demonstrates strong NJ demand signal.
stories.summary: Vango Development has opened leasing at Parker East, a five-story luxury rental community with 86 residences in East Rutherford, New Jersey, located 0.2 miles from the Rutherford NJ TRANSIT station. One- and two-bedroom units are priced from $3,250 with immediate occupancy. This is Vango's third development in the Rutherford area, following Parker 106 and Parker 118.
stories.impact: Strong demand signal for transit-oriented multifamily in the Hudson County/NJ Transit corridor. Successful lease-up and expansion of Vango's Rutherford footprint validate the rent absorption and market receptivity for commuter housing near Manhattan access points—developers should prioritize similar transit nodes across North Jersey for mid-rise product.

stories.excerpt: M&T Realty Capital Corporation closed on a $31.9-million bridge loan for Estelle New Haven, a newly constructed 96-unit Class A multifamily community located at 19 Elm St. in downtown New Haven, CT. The financing will support the property’s continued lease-up and stabilization while refinancing existing construction debt. Developed by Eight West, an affiliate of The Hakimian Organization, Estelle New Haven is a seven-story mixed-use development featuring 96 residential units and approximately 1,500 square feet of ground-floor retail space. It’s located near Yale University and New Haven’s transit network. “Estelle reflects our long-term commitment to creating high-quality multifamily communities that contribute to the growth and vitality of the neighborhoods in which we invest,” said Jay Hakimian, principal of Eight West. “We are grateful for M&T RCC’s support throughout the process and proud to deliver a community that will provide residents with an exceptional living experience while contributing to the continued revitalization of downtown New Haven.” The post ... appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: M&T RCC closes $31.9M bridge loan for Estelle New Haven: 96-unit Class A downtown.
Eight West developed mixed-use project near Yale; bridge supports lease-up and stabilization.
Ground-floor retail and Yale proximity anchor demand in downtown revitalization play.
stories.summary: M&T Realty Capital Corporation closed a $31.9 million bridge loan for Estelle New Haven, a newly constructed 96-unit Class A multifamily community developed by Eight West (Hakimian Organization affiliate) at 19 Elm Street in downtown New Haven. The seven-story mixed-use development includes approximately 1,500 square feet of ground-floor retail and is located near Yale University and the city's transit network. The financing supports lease-up and stabilization while refinancing existing construction debt.
stories.impact: Bridge financing at scale signals ongoing investor confidence in Yale-anchored New Haven downtown revitalization. Strong institutional financing availability for Class A lease-up projects suggests cap rates and construction debt refinancing remain workable; developers should monitor downtown New Haven for additional infill and adaptive reuse opportunities tied to Yale expansion and transit connectivity.

stories.title: Drawbridge Extends Full-Building Lease with Microsoft Unit in Santa Clara
stories.excerpt: Drawbridge Realty has extended a lease with Microsoft for the entire 66,106-square-foot Class A office building located at 3201 Scott Boulevard in Santa Clara. The property has been home to Fungible, Inc., which was acquired by Microsoft in 2023, since 2016. Drawbridge acquired 3201 Scott Boulevard in 2012 and subsequently completed a significant renovation of the property.  “We’re delighted to be able to provide Microsoft with continuity and quality workspace at 3201 Scott Boulevard well into the next decade,” said Mike Embree, Chief Portfolio Officer, Drawbridge Realty.   The two-story building sits on 3.5 acres at the intersection of Scott Boulevard and San Tomas Expressway. Jeff Cushman and Walt Stephenson of Cushman & Wakefield represented Drawbridge Realty in lease renewal negotiations. Alex Lagemann of JLL represented Microsoft. The post Drawbridge Extends Full-Building Lease with Microsoft Unit in Santa Clara appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Microsoft extends full-building lease at 3201 Scott Blvd, Santa Clara: 66,106 SF office.
Building formerly home to Fungible, Inc., acquired by Microsoft in 2023.
Tech firm commitment validates Santa Clara market resilience despite broader Bay Area softness.
stories.summary: Drawbridge Realty extended a lease with Microsoft for the entire 66,106-square-foot Class A office building at 3201 Scott Boulevard in Santa Clara, California. The property has housed Fungible, Inc. (acquired by Microsoft in 2023) since 2016. Drawbridge acquired the two-story building on 3.5 acres in 2012 and completed a significant renovation.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, Microsoft's full-building commitment signals durability of Santa Clara as a tech employment anchor and validates continued demand for Class A office near major transit. Developers in the Bay Area should monitor corporate consolidations—large tech M&A driving headcount and talent migration can create multifamily demand in satellite submarkets around major employers' HQs and R&D campuses.

stories.title: Wonderful Real Estate Trades 1.1M-SF Industrial to Global Technology Company
stories.excerpt: The Wonderful Company announced that its Wonderful Real Estate business has completed the sale of 5104 Express Ave. to a major global technology and e-commerce company. The newly constructed 1,088,047-square-foot, Class A industrial facility is located at the Wonderful Logistics Center in Shafter and marks the buyer’s third location at the 2,000-acre, fully entitled, master-planned logistics and distribution campus, bringing its owned and leased footprint to more than three million square feet. “Global operators continue to choose Wonderful Logistics Center because we are a model within the state and the country that offers something fundamentally different,” said Joe Vargas, president of Wonderful Real Estate. “Nowhere else is there a master-planned logistics hub that brings together large-scale distribution, workforce and community development and the future of clean freight infrastructure. This buyer’s continued investment validates the strength of Wonderful Logistics Center as one of California’s leading models for responsible logistics and durable economic growth that benefits businesses, workers and communities alike.” In 2025, the buyer also partnered with Bakersfield College and The Wonderful Company to launch a 12-week Mechatronics & Robotics Apprenticeship program for U.S. employees at the on-site Wonderful Career Center, providing hands-on, SACA-certified training to prepare employees for skilled technical roles and career advancement. To date, more than 100 student employees have graduated from the program and entered year-long apprenticeships before they transition into mid-level technical roles at the company. The post Wonderful Real Estate Trades 1.1M-SF Industrial to Global Technology Company appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Wonderful Real Estate sells 1.09M SF industrial in Shafter to global tech/e-commerce firm.
Buyer's third location at Wonderful Logistics Center; total footprint exceeds 3M SF.
Master-planned logistics campus anchors Kern County industrial demand; reflects supply-chain durability.
stories.summary: The Wonderful Company completed the sale of 5104 Express Avenue, a newly constructed 1,088,047-square-foot Class A industrial facility at the Wonderful Logistics Center in Shafter, California, to a major global technology and e-commerce company. This marks the buyer's third location at the 2,000-acre master-planned logistics hub, bringing its total footprint to more than three million square feet. The buyer is also partnering on a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprenticeship program with Bakersfield College.
stories.impact: Indirect signal for multifamily in Kern County. Large-scale industrial consolidation and workforce development initiatives at Wonderful Logistics Center will drive sustained job creation and population in-migration to Bakersfield/Shafter corridor. Developers should assess rental demand from logistics/distribution workforce (typically lower-income, family-oriented) in secondary markets around major master-planned industrial parks—opportunity to develop workforce housing products near job clusters.

stories.title: CIBC Supplies $102M Refi for SkyREM Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Real estate investment firm SkyREM has secured $101.8 million to refinance a 1.9 million-square-foot industrial portfolio across the East Coast, Commercial Observer has learned. CIBC provided the nonrecourse financing, which carries an initial three-year term with two one-year extension options. JLL Capital Markets’ Peter Rotchford, Steven Binswanger and Lucas Borges arranged the transaction on behalf of SkyREM. “This financing reflects the strength of the portfolio and gives us additional flexibility to continue investing in well-located industrial assets where we see compelling long-term value,” SkyREM CEO Alexander Dembitzer said in a statement. The industrial portfolio spans four properties and is 100 percent occupied by six tenants, according to JLL. The East Coast properties, located in Georgia, Florida, and South Carolina, serve a range of warehousing, manufacturing and e-commerce uses. SkyREM, which holds dual offices in New York City and Philadelphia, owns and operates 30 properties across a largely industrial U.S. portfolio, according to its website. The firm counts Lockheed Martin, FedEx, Amazon and Shein among its major tenants. SkyREM most recently acquired a 325,334-square-foot manufacturing facility in Casa Grand, Ariz., according to a January release. In early 2025, the firm secured a $170 million refinancing for a 10-building, 2.5 million-square-foot portfolio. That loan was provided by affiliates of Apollo, and was also arranged by JLL. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CIBC provides $101.8M nonrecourse refi for SkyREM's 1.9M SF industrial portfolio.
Four properties across Georgia, Florida, South Carolina; 100% leased by six tenants.
Three-year term with two one-year extension options signals lender comfort with logistics assets.
stories.summary: SkyREM secured $101.8 million in nonrecourse financing from CIBC to refinance a 1.9 million-square-foot industrial portfolio across four properties in Georgia, Florida, and South Carolina. The portfolio is 100 percent occupied by six tenants serving warehousing, manufacturing, and e-commerce uses. The loan carries an initial three-year term with two one-year extension options. JLL Capital Markets arranged the transaction.
stories.impact: Refinancing signal of debt market strength for core industrial assets in Sunbelt logistics markets (GA, FL, SC). Availability of nonrecourse capital at scale validates supply-chain and distribution-driven demand durability. Multifamily developers should recognize that strong industrial fundamentals in these markets (occupancy, tenant credit) support broader economic confidence and population in-migration—time to underwrite multifamily in industrial-adjacent submarkets with workforce housing gaps.

stories.title: As Fed Hikes Rates for First Time Since 2023, Commercial Real Estate Comes to Terms
stories.excerpt: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years Wednesday, but the hawkish move is not expected to curtail commercial real estate transactions in the latter half of 2026. In a unanimous 12-0 vote, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) hiked its benchmark interest rate a quarter point to between 3.75 percent and 4 percent, noting continued inflationary pressures that have been compounded by the war in Iran. The move followed five straight rate holds and marked the central bank’s first time increasing borrowing costs since July 2023. The Fed also released its updated quarterly “dot plot” matrix of individual committee members, which signaled an additional rate hike later this year would likely be supported by 16 of 18 FOMC participants. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has not participated in the dot plot exercise since taking over the leadership post in June. “The plain fact is that inflation is too high, and has been for too long,” Warsh said in a post-meeting press conference. “This summer’s inflation readings do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.” The FOMC said it remains committed to maintaining the board’s long-standing inflation goal of a 2 percent annual rate, and that recent data put the rate well above this target. The Fed’s dot plot grid projected the federal funds rate at 4.1 percent for the end of 2026 and remain at that level through 2027. Since assuming the Fed chair post from Jerome Powell, Warsh has presided over two pauses and one rate hike in his first three meetings as Fed chair despite external pressure from President Donald Trump, who nominated Warsh in January. In a Sept. 4 Truth Social post, Trump called on the Fed to cut interest rates or he would stop trading with certain countries. bullets: Federal Reserve raises rates 25 bps to 3.75–4% range; first hike since July 2023.
16 of 18 FOMC participants signal support for additional 2026 rate increase.
Inflation cited as driver; market not expected to curtail CRE activity in H2 2026.
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points to between 3.75 and 4 percent in a unanimous 12-0 FOMC vote, marking the first hike since July 2023. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh cited persistent inflationary pressures compounded by geopolitical factors. The dot plot matrix indicated that 16 of 18 FOMC participants support an additional rate hike later in 2026. Despite the hawkish move, commercial real estate transactions are not expected to slow in the latter half of 2026.
stories.impact: Rate-hike cycle inflection point: multifamily underwriting models and refinance assumptions must reset. Higher-for-longer rate regime will compress valuations, widen cap rates, and reduce leverage availability. Developers should frontload construction financing locks and recalibrate cost-of-capital assumptions in underwriting; acquisition windows may compress as cap rates widen and capital sources retreat to lower-risk assets. Expect acquisition cap rates to move 50–100 bps higher over next 6–12 months.

stories.title: Law Firm Greenberg Traurig Expands to 133K SF at One Vanderbilt
stories.excerpt: Law firm Greenberg Traurig has no objections to its Midtown offices at One Vanderbilt — in fact, it’s taking even more space there. The law firm, which provides legal services to businesses, financial institutions and high-profile individuals, has signed a 10.5-year lease for 33,477 additional square feet on the entire 33rd floor of SL Green Realty’s trophy high-rise at 1 Vanderbilt Avenue, according to the landlord. The lease brings Greenberg’s total office footprint at the skyscraper to 133,365 square feet. Greenberg signed its initial 15-year lease for four contiguous floors at One Vanderbilt in January 2018, before the 1.7 million-square-foot office tower was completed in 2020. The law firm moved from its previous offices at the MetLife Building at 200 Park Avenue, where its lease expired in 2021. The asking rent for the firm’s new expansion lease at One Vanderbilt was not disclosed, but Steven Durels, executive vice president and director of leasing and real property at SL Green, told Commercial Observer in February that rents in the building range from between $250 to “well over $300” per square foot. “Strong leasing momentum continues unabated with many tenants expanding and making significant capital investment to provide upscale work environments to better recruit and retain employee talent,” Durels said in a statement. CBRE’s Michael Monahan and Mark Ravesloot brokered the deal for Greenberg, while it’s unclear whether SL Green had any representation. Spokespeople for CBRE and Greenberg did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Greenberg’s expansion keeps One Vanderbilt at 100 percent leased. Other office tenants include TD Bank, investment management firm Carlyle Group, alternative investment firm Oak Hill Advisors and SL Green itself. News of the deal also comes during a recent wave of office leasing for SL Green, which said it has signed 129 office leases in Manhattan totaling 1.8 million square feet so far in 2026. bullets: Greenberg Traurig expands to 133K SF at One Vanderbilt, Midtown NYC; 10.5-year lease.
Law firm takes additional 33,477 SF (entire 33rd floor); total now 133,365 SF.
High-profile tenant retention signals trophy office leasing strength despite macro softness.
stories.summary: Law firm Greenberg Traurig signed a 10.5-year lease for an additional 33,477 square feet—the entire 33rd floor—at SL Green Realty's One Vanderbilt, a 1.7 million-square-foot trophy office tower in Midtown Manhattan. The expansion brings Greenberg's total footprint in the building to 133,365 square feet. The firm originally signed a 15-year lease for four contiguous floors in January 2018 before the building's 2020 completion.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, Greenberg's expansion at One Vanderbilt signals that Manhattan's trophy Class A office market for high-margin service firms (legal, finance) remains resilient and commands premium rents. This may slow adaptive-reuse conversion of Midtown office into multifamily; focus conversion efforts on secondary/tertiary office stock rather than Class A core. Monitor whether office lease expansion in Midtown correlates with compressed multifamily supply growth in Manhattan.

stories.title: In Pro-Development South Florida, NIMBYism Rises
stories.excerpt: When Catherine Adler first moved to the West Palm Beach area in 1991, the South Florida city counted only a handful of high-rises, most of which were clustered around downtown. Today, though, she barely recognizes the regional city. Since 2019, at least nine towers have been completed. More than 10 are now under construction, some rising in residential neighborhoods packed with single-family homes. And more change is likely to come: Another nine developments have already been approved. “There’s cranes everywhere. You turn around and, all of a sudden, something’s going up,” Adler said. “The beautiful waterfront, the historic neighborhoods, and the charm — I don’t know if that’s going to be around.” South Florida has long been a bastion of new development. For decades, the region prospered thanks to pro-development policies that fueled a boom in condominium construction that attracted vacationers, retirees, foreign investors looking for a second home and wealthy newcomers. But, in recent years, South Florida has faced an all-too familiar obstacle: NIMBYism. The “Not In My Back Yard” phenomenon has long been common in places with starkly different politics, such as New York and California, but after years of developer free-for-all, NIMBYism has now finally descended onto South Florida. “We might be reaching a turning point,” said David Foster, an assistant professor at Florida State University who studies the politics of housing. “There’s nothing inherently partisan or conservative or liberal necessarily about homeowners’ opposition to development.” While South Florida, like most regions, has had its share of NIMBYism over the years, the movement is gaining significant steam since the COVID-19 pandemic, when millions of Northeasterners moved south to Florida. bullets: West Palm Beach has completed 9+ towers since 2019; 10+ under construction.
NIMBYism rising in pro-development South Florida region; neighborhood resistance to density.
9 additional developments already approved; zoning and community pushback may slow delivery.
stories.summary: West Palm Beach has experienced rapid residential densification, with at least nine towers completed since 2019 and over 10 currently under construction, many in residential neighborhoods of single-family homes. An additional nine developments have already been approved. Long-time residents cite concerns over loss of historic character and waterfront charm, signaling a shift toward NIMBYism in what has been a traditionally pro-development market. Catherine Adler, a resident since 1991, notes the dramatic transformation and uncertainty about the region's future.
stories.impact: Critical entitlement headwind for South Florida multifamily developers. Rising local opposition threatens approval timelines and may drive up soft costs (community benefits, extended permitting). Developers should prioritize already-entitled sites or downtown corridors with less neighborhood friction (e.g., West Palm Beach downtown infill vs. residential edge neighborhoods). Monitor West Palm Beach city council and zoning board activity; anticipate higher per-unit soft costs and longer delivery timelines as NIMBY resistance hardens—consider value-add conversions or build-to-rent strategies to mitigate neighborhood opposition risk.

stories.title: George Soros Puts Argonaut Building on the Market for Roughly $100M
stories.excerpt: Another Manhattan office building has hit the market. This time it’s the landmarked Argonaut Building, an approximately 140,000-square-foot office and retail building at 224 West 57th Street in Midtown. George Soros’s Soros Fund Management has put the property up for sale and is seeking a price of roughly $100 million, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. The 1909-built building between Broadway and Seventh Avenue seems to be fully occupied by Soros’s grant-making group the Open Society Foundations, which moved into the building in 2013 and has a lease running through 2042. TD Bank is a retail tenant on the ground floor. In April 2024, Soros, as a tenant, filed a foreclosure lawsuit against former landlord eretz group citing a default on a $145 million mortgage, The Real Deal reported at the time. Eretz had purchased the site for $213.8 million in 2015. It’s unclear why Soros is now looking to offload the property after winning it in a foreclosure auction, but the billionaire plans to move his grant-making group from the building once a deal is closed, according to TRD, which first reported the listing news. Newmark’s Adam Spies, Adam Doneger and Willis Robbins are marketing the building. An offering memo from the brokerage said the sale is a “rare opportunity” to reposition the historic building into “best-in-class residences,” TRD reported. The property has additional air rights that could give it a total buildable space of more than 200,000 square feet, according to the publication. If an office-to-residential conversion does proceed at the West 57th Street building, it would join another conversion project nearby at 135 East 57th Street, where TF Cornerstone is turning the former office building into 350 apartments. Newmark declined to comment, while a spokesperson for Open Society Foundations did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Isabelle Durso can be reached at idurso@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: George Soros sells landmarked Argonaut Building, Manhattan, for ~$100M.
140K SF office/retail on West 57th Street; Open Society Foundations lease through 2042.
Soros exiting office ownership post-foreclosure; office conversion risk remains limited.
stories.summary: George Soros's Soros Fund Management has put the landmarked Argonaut Building, a 140,000-square-foot office and retail property at 224 West 57th Street in Midtown Manhattan, on the market for approximately $100 million. The 1909-built building is fully occupied by the Open Society Foundations (which moved in 2013) under a lease through 2042, with TD Bank occupying ground-floor retail. Soros acquired the property in a foreclosure auction after the previous owner defaulted on a $145 million mortgage.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily opportunity. The 62-year lease to Open Society Foundations and landmarked status severely restrict adaptive reuse for residential. Office values in Midtown remain depressed (~$714/SF asking), signaling oversupply, but conversion economics do not work on long-term-leased Class B space. Developers should focus multifamily conversion opportunities on unleveraged, shorter-lease office with higher extinction risk—not long-term-anchored buildings. The $100M ask for 140K SF (~$714/SF) reflects persistent Midtown office distress, a valuation benchmark for multifamily acquisition targets.
